title: How Many Rooms
statement: An office books meetings as `[start, end]` minute pairs. A meeting uses its room from `start` up to, but not including, `end`, so a meeting ending at 10 and one starting at 10 can share a room. Return the smallest number of rooms needed for all meetings.

answerKey.pattern: Sort by start time; min-heap of end times of rooms in use
keyPoints: Process meetings in order of start time
The heap holds the end time of each room in use; its root is the room that frees up first
If the earliest end is <= the new start, reuse that room (pop)
Push the new meeting's end; the largest heap size is the answer
edgeCases: Back-to-back meetings that share a room
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Separate sorted start and end lists with two pointers: also O(n log n)
Check every minute: far too slow

hints: Go through meetings by start time. When a new meeting starts, which room could it reuse?
The room that frees up earliest. Keep the end times of busy rooms in a min-heap.
Pop while the earliest end is <= the new start (one pop is enough), push the new end, and track the heap's largest size.
